content: User-submitted photos routinely carry embedded EXIF metadata (GPS coordinates, device ID, precise timestamp) that itself counts as personal data under GDPR/PDPA-equivalent regimes, independent of visible faces in the image. Organizations that redact visible faces but forget to strip EXIF metadata remain non-compliant and may retain geolocation data they are legally obligated to delete on request. Storage-limitation principle requires retention periods tied to purpose, not operational convenience, and 'right to be forgotten' must reach all copies (including any raw/backup storage), not just the served version.
